Lessons.Title: Number Talk
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply your understanding of addition and subtraction to create a Number Talk activity.
This lesson provides an opportunity to observe the ways in which you make use of structure and repeated reasoning to design a Number Talk. The warm-up is followed by four Number Talk activities. In the first activity, you are given three expressions and asked to write the missing expression.

Warm-up Number Talk: Addition (10 minutes). Mental products are not involved. Compute 300 + 400 = 700, 300 + 437 = 737, 321 + 437 = 758, and 425 + 514 = 939, using place value and connections between nearby expressions.

Activity 1 Number Talk Design 1 (15 minutes): consider subtraction 600 − 400 = 200, 600 − 399 = 201, and 500 − 399 = 101. Find at least two mental strategies for each, then author a fourth subtraction expression that benefits from a related strategy.
Activity 2 Number Talk Design 2 (15 minutes): consider 500 + 199 = 699 and 504 + 199 = 703, explain two mental strategies and write two additional related sums supporting the same approaches.
Activity 3 Number Talk Design 3 (15 minutes): begin with 900 − 400 = 500 and write three more subtraction expressions to complete a connected Number Talk.

Activity 4 Number Talk Design 4 (15 minutes): independently choose four addition or subtraction expressions whose values are accessible through mental patterns; explain why the chosen sequence highlights structure.

The teacher facilitates and reviews students' original designed sequences, multiple valid strategies and discussion. Publisher-gated Number Talk Reflection Cool-down has not been viewed or reproduced.
Source-authentic activity scripts are teacher mediated. Figures, print-only masters and publisher-gated Cool-downs not independently inspected are not claimed source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Preserved valid source-bound concepts
KeyConcepts.Definition:
Key ideas:
- Apply understanding of addition and subtraction within 1,000 to create a Number Talk activity
- This lesson provides an opportunity to observe the ways in which you make use of structure and repeated reasoning to design a Number Talk
- Subtraction can represent taking away, comparing quantities, or finding a missing addend; the representation must match the situation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use in conjunction with the individually verified 2021 activity directions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Learning goal: You will apply your understanding of addition and subtraction to create a Number Talk activity.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mental computation within 1,000
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use place value and compensation to calculate without a written algorithm.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Decompose hundreds, tens and ones; check relationships.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compensation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Change an addend or subtrahend by one and adjust the result accordingly.

KeyConcepts.Title: Number Talk design
KeyConcepts.Definition: Sequence related expressions so a previous solution helps the next.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Include more than one explanatory strategy, not a list of isolated sums.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open student authorship
KeyConcepts.Definition: Learners create additional expressions for peers.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher evaluates the mathematical connection between chosen expressions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Start with 900−400 and extend with related differences.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original public warm-up sums
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 300+400, 300+437, 321+437 and 425+514.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compensation in a subtraction talk
WorkedExamples.Question: Use 600−400 to find 600−399, then compare 500−399.
Steps: Subtracting one less (399 instead of 400) raises the result by one to 201.
Changing 600 to 500 reduces the difference by 100: 101.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compensation in an addition talk
WorkedExamples.Question: Connect the original expressions 500 + 199 and 504 + 199 without a written algorithm.
WorkedExamples.Method: Independent first-party source-aligned reasoning; not a copy of the publisher's original image or student-authored work
Steps: Raise the first addend by four: 504 + 199 = 703; explain the student-authored follow-up.
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher separately checks the original source, pupil drawing or physical activity; this illustration is not an original-source parity certificate.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Subtracting one less than 400 should increase 600−400=200 by one.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ignoring that 504+199 is four more than 500+199.
Mistaking teacher-reviewed designed expressions for fixed numerical answer keys.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks students to invent three/four appropriate expressions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher evaluates mathematical connectedness and reasoning.
